A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inhibition of BSEP is only one of many potential causes of cholestasis and hepatotoxicity, which can be drug induced.
the inhibition of BSEP alone is not sufficient to cause cholestatis and hepatotoxicity.
the inhibition of BSEP is only a part of the story, and that the overall BA pool and EHR must be considered when assessing the hepatotoxicity potential of a drug.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a drug-induced cholestatic response can be the consequence of multiple mechanisms, and the identification of the underlying mechanism(s) is critical for risk assessment and for the development of appropriate mitigation strategies.
the inhibition of BA transporters, BA sulfation, and BA amidation can be used as biomarkers to identify compounds that are cholestasis risk candidates.
